world.title: ICC unseals warrants for four Taliban leaders over gender persecution
world.summary: The International Criminal Court on Oct. 5 made public arrest warrants for Taliban supreme leader Haibatullah Akhundzada, Supreme Court chief Abdul Hakim Haqqani, Education Minister Habibullah Agha and Higher Education Minister Neda Mohammad Nadim, accusing them of crimes against humanity through gender-based persecuti
world.content: The International Criminal Court on Oct. 5 made public arrest warrants for Taliban supreme leader Haibatullah Akhundzada, Supreme Court chief Abdul Hakim Haqqani, Education Minister Habibullah Agha and Higher Education Minister Neda Mohammad Nadim, accusing them of crimes against humanity through gender-based persecution in Afghanistan. The court said there were reasonable grounds to believe the four ordered, induced or solicited the persecution of women and girls, people whose gender identity or expression conflicted with Taliban policy, and people viewed as their allies. The alleged crimes spanned the period from the Taliban’s return to power on Aug. 15, 2021, through at least Jan. 20, 2025. The court issued the warrants for Akhundzada and Haqqani in July 2025 and those for Agha and Nadim in September 2025; all had remained sealed until the court’s decision. Judges said Taliban policies severely restricted fundamental rights and linked the alleged persecution to acts including murder, imprisonment, torture, rape and enforced disappearance. The ICC said unsealing the warrants would not unduly affect its ongoing investigations and could encourage international cooperation. The court has no police force, and the suspects remain at large; enforcement depends on states cooperating with the ICC. Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid said Afghanistan does not recognize the court’s authority.
world.image_alt: ICC unseals warrants for four Taliban leaders over gender persecution

world.title: Bestselling British novelist Jeffrey Archer dies at 86 before final novel’s publication
world.summary: British novelist and former Conservative politician Jeffrey Archer died Monday at 86, publisher HarperCollins said. His final novel, “Adam and Eve,” was scheduled for publication Tuesday, Oct. 6. Archer’s books sold more than 300 million copies worldwide, including the thrillers “Kane & Abel” and “Not a Penny More, Not
world.content: British novelist and former Conservative politician Jeffrey Archer died Monday at 86, publisher HarperCollins said. His final novel, “Adam and Eve,” was scheduled for publication Tuesday, Oct. 6. Archer’s books sold more than 300 million copies worldwide, including the thrillers “Kane & Abel” and “Not a Penny More, Not a Penny Less”. Archer was elected to Parliament in 1969 and later became Conservative Party deputy chairman under Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher. His political career was derailed when a jury found he had lied in a libel case against the Daily Star. He had sued the newspaper over a 1987 allegation and won £500,000, but in 2001 was convicted of perjury and perverting the course of justice. He received a four-year sentence and served about two years in prison. Archer returned to the House of Lords after his release and retired in 2024. The day before his death, he appeared at London’s Leicester Square Theatre to sign books and discuss “Adam and Eve.” He had been due to discuss the novel at the Cheltenham Literature Festival later in the week.
world.image_alt: Bestselling British novelist Jeffrey Archer dies at 86 before final novel’s publication

world.title: Yemen
world.summary: Yemen’s Houthi movement said Monday, Oct. 5, that it had launched missiles and drones at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, an Aramco refinery in Rabigh and other Saudi sites as Saudi-backed forces pressed a campaign to retake Houthi-held territory. Saudi Arabia did not confirm the claimed direct hits; explos
world.content: Yemen’s Houthi movement said Monday, Oct. 5, that it had launched missiles and drones at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, an Aramco refinery in Rabigh and other Saudi sites as Saudi-backed forces pressed a campaign to retake Houthi-held territory. Saudi Arabia did not confirm the claimed direct hits; explosions were heard in Riyadh, while King Khalid remained open despite flight delays. Yemen’s internationally recognized government announced the offensive on Sunday, saying its forces had carried out more than 1,000 strikes. The Saudi-led coalition said about 100 aircraft flew missions and reported strikes on Houthi military targets near Hodeidah. Riyadh, Islamabad and Ankara agreed to arrange the rapid deployment of forces and capabilities covered by their mutual-defense pact, but did not specify what roles those forces would play. The Houthis seized Red Sea coastline near the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, a key maritime corridor, last month and have attacked Saudi shipping and oil infrastructure. The UN says more than 184,000 people have been displaced. A Saudi energy-sector source said an attack Sunday again halted pumping through the East-West pipeline, while Aramco chief executive Amin Nasser warned that global oil stocks were “scarily thin”.

world.title: Israeli officials say Flydubai co-pilot planned airport attack before joining airline
world.summary: Israeli officials say the Flydubai co-pilot accused of attacking the captain told Emirati interrogators he planned the attack before joining the airline and sought work with a carrier that flew to Tel Aviv. A source briefed on the UAE inquiry said he intended to crash Flight FZ1073 at Ben Gurion Airport. Israeli offici
world.content: Israeli officials say the Flydubai co-pilot accused of attacking the captain told Emirati interrogators he planned the attack before joining the airline and sought work with a carrier that flew to Tel Aviv. A source briefed on the UAE inquiry said he intended to crash Flight FZ1073 at Ben Gurion Airport. Israeli officials have not publicly identified him, but sources have named him as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami. The same source said the co-pilot had considered hijacking an earlier Tel Aviv-bound flight this year but abandoned the plan, possibly because someone he knew was aboard. U.S. Vice President JD Vance said he had seen nothing conclusive indicating an Iranian role. The United Arab Emirates continues to lead the investigation with security agencies from regional countries and assistance from the United States and other Western governments. The inquiry is also examining the suspect’s overseas background. New Zealand police said he was in the country from November 2018 to May 2019 on a student visa to complete part of his flight training for a U.K.-based company.
world.image_alt: Israeli officials say Flydubai co-pilot planned airport attack before joining airline

world.title: Spain’s Sánchez calls November 29 election after housing bill defeat
world.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap election for Nov. 29, bringing the vote forward from 2027 after parliament rejected his government’s housing decrees on Friday, Oct. 2. The proposals included automatic renewal of rental contracts, limits on evicting vulnerable tenants and restrictions on investment fu
world.content: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap election for Nov. 29, bringing the vote forward from 2027 after parliament rejected his government’s housing decrees on Friday, Oct. 2. The proposals included automatic renewal of rental contracts, limits on evicting vulnerable tenants and restrictions on investment funds buying homes; opposition parties and Catalan separatist party Junts voted them down. The defeat followed nationwide demonstrations over housing costs, intensified by the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from her Madrid home. Sánchez said he wants voters to give him broader parliamentary support to pursue reforms. “To do more, we need to renew and broaden the support of the people,” he said. The conservative People’s Party (PP) leads Sánchez’s Socialists in polls but may need support from far-right Vox to form a government. Sánchez’s minority coalition has struggled to pass legislation, and Spain has not approved a national budget since 2023. The decree calling the election was due to be published in Spain’s Official State Gazette on Oct. 6, starting the statutory 54-day election period.
world.image_alt: Spain’s Sánchez calls November 29 election after housing bill defeat

world.title: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye activate pact, prepare force deployment
world.summary: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye agreed on Oct. 5 to implement their mutual-defense commitments and arrange the rapid deployment of agreed forces and military capabilities in the kingdom after an emergency meeting of their alliance committee in Riyadh. The three countries signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in
world.content: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye agreed on Oct. 5 to implement their mutual-defense commitments and arrange the rapid deployment of agreed forces and military capabilities in the kingdom after an emergency meeting of their alliance committee in Riyadh. The three countries signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in August; it treats an armed attack on one member as an attack on all. The decision followed escalating fighting in Yemen. The Saudi-backed government announced a counteroffensive to retake Houthi-held territory. The alliance statement condemned attacks on Saudi cities and civilian and economic facilities, as well as attempts to target Makkah and Madinah, without naming the Houthis. The joint statement gave no deployment schedule or detailed mission. Pakistan’s Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said Saudi troops were conducting combat operations while Pakistani and Turkish forces played supportive roles, with Pakistani forces conducting reconnaissance. The deployment is to follow approved arrangements and each country’s laws.
world.image_alt: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye activate pact, prepare force deployment

world.title: Quebec separatists win minority government, revive independence referendum push
world.summary: Quebec’s Parti Québécois won the provincial election on Oct. 5, returning to power after more than a decade but falling short of a majority. The party was on track to take nearly 60 of the 127 seats in the National Assembly, short of the 64 needed for a majority. Leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon has promised another ind
world.content: Quebec’s Parti Québécois won the provincial election on Oct. 5, returning to power after more than a decade but falling short of a majority. The party was on track to take nearly 60 of the 127 seats in the National Assembly, short of the 64 needed for a majority. Leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon has promised another independence referendum but says he will wait until U.S. President Donald Trump leaves office. Trump’s term is scheduled to end in January 2029. As a minority government, the PQ will need opposition support to pass legislation and survive confidence votes. Polls put support for sovereignty at about 30%. Political scientist Daniel Béland said the election reflected voter discontent with the outgoing Coalition Avenir Québec government rather than a decisive mandate to leave Canada. Prime Minister Mark Carney congratulated St-Pierre Plamondon and said Ottawa would work with the incoming government. Albertans are due to vote on Oct. 19 on whether to begin the process toward a separation referendum.
world.image_alt: Quebec separatists win minority government, revive independence referendum push

world.title: French unions join nationwide student protests after teenager loses hand
world.summary: French student and education unions called for nationwide demonstrations Tuesday, with up to 40,000 people expected in Paris, after a 15-year-old lost a hand when a police grenade exploded during clashes in Lens on Monday. The teenager was taken to hospital, and his condition was not life-threatening. Authorities opene
world.content: French student and education unions called for nationwide demonstrations Tuesday, with up to 40,000 people expected in Paris, after a 15-year-old lost a hand when a police grenade exploded during clashes in Lens on Monday. The teenager was taken to hospital, and his condition was not life-threatening. Authorities opened an investigation, while accounts differ over whether he picked up the device or was struck by it. Teacher unions, university students and other groups have backed the demonstrations, and authorities expected disruptions at 30 to 40 higher-education sites. Organisers say the government has not offered concrete steps to address teacher shortages, crowded classes and deteriorating schools. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has directed ministers to develop proposals by the end of October. The Education Ministry said protests or disruptions affected 413 schools on Monday, 27% fewer than at the same point on Friday. At least 190 students had been injured since the movement began. Six judicial investigations into police use of force have been opened, according to Le Monde.
world.image_alt: French unions join nationwide student protests after teenager loses hand

business.title: India and US trade talks stall as room for concessions narrows
business.summary: India’s trade negotiations with the United States have reached a “plateau,” Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said, warning that further compromise could be very difficult even as talks continue. The two countries have yet to resolve the terms of a proposed agreement. An initial understanding announced in February ou
business.content: India’s trade negotiations with the United States have reached a “plateau,” Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said, warning that further compromise could be very difficult even as talks continue. The two countries have yet to resolve the terms of a proposed agreement. An initial understanding announced in February outlined plans for Washington to cut tariffs to 18% and India to reduce duties on a range of industrial and agricultural products. Unresolved issues include a U.S. investigation into alleged unfair trade practices involving India and other countries. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said last week that an announcement was not imminent and that negotiators had identified the sticking points. Sitharaman said there was still room for both sides to operate.
business.image_alt: India and US trade talks stall as room for concessions narrows

business.title: Huawei licenses Qualcomm patents across 5G, AI and chip technologies
business.summary: Huawei and Qualcomm signed a multi-year patent agreement covering 5G, computing, artificial intelligence and networking. It includes Qualcomm’s purchase of certain Huawei U.S. patents and a license to Huawei’s LogicFolding chip technology. The companies did not disclose financial terms. Huawei said the agreement would
business.content: Huawei and Qualcomm signed a multi-year patent agreement covering 5G, computing, artificial intelligence and networking. It includes Qualcomm’s purchase of certain Huawei U.S. patents and a license to Huawei’s LogicFolding chip technology. The companies did not disclose financial terms. Huawei said the agreement would bring the cumulative value of its patent-licensing contracts to more than $6.9 billion once the deal closes. The cross-license is the first agreement between the companies to cover 5G patents, according to Reuters reporting carried by Slashdot. The deal requires regulatory approvals; a report citing Bloomberg said it is subject to U.S. Federal Trade Commission review under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act. The agreement covers Qualcomm’s wireless patents and Huawei’s intellectual property in computing, AI and networking.

business.title: TalkTalk creditors face losses as BT rescue deal awaits review
business.summary: TalkTalk’s creditors are likely to be left with unpaid claims totalling hundreds of millions of pounds after BT’s purchase of the broadband group’s businesses through a pre-pack administration. Shareholders, including founder Charles Dunstone, are expected to be wiped out. BT is acquiring the businesses debt-free, but
business.content: TalkTalk’s creditors are likely to be left with unpaid claims totalling hundreds of millions of pounds after BT’s purchase of the broadband group’s businesses through a pre-pack administration. Shareholders, including founder Charles Dunstone, are expected to be wiped out. BT is acquiring the businesses debt-free, but TalkTalk had about £1.5 billion of debt and was loss-making. The transaction still faces regulatory scrutiny. The Competition and Markets Authority is due to report by 19 October on competition concerns, after which Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy can consider the wider public interest. BT and TalkTalk must remain separate and compete during the review. Virgin Media O2 has challenged the arrangement as unfair to competition, while Ofcom says existing obligations remain in force and it will monitor the transition.
business.image_alt: TalkTalk creditors face losses as BT rescue deal awaits review

business.title: Schneider Electric agrees to buy PTC for $22.6 billion
business.summary: Schneider Electric agreed to acquire U.S. industrial software maker PTC for $22.6 billion in equity value, or $205 a share in cash; including debt, the transaction values PTC at $23.7 billion. The French company said the combination would expand its industrial software and artificial-intelligence business by connecting
business.content: Schneider Electric agreed to acquire U.S. industrial software maker PTC for $22.6 billion in equity value, or $205 a share in cash; including debt, the transaction values PTC at $23.7 billion. The French company said the combination would expand its industrial software and artificial-intelligence business by connecting software and product data across design, manufacturing, operation and maintenance. Schneider expects €250 million in annual cost savings by the third year after closing and about €800 million in additional revenue from the combination. It expects to finance the purchase by issuing up to €17 billion in new debt and up to €6 billion in new shares. The deal requires shareholder and regulatory approvals and is expected to close by the third quarter of 2027.
business.image_alt: Schneider Electric agrees to buy PTC for $22.6 billion

business.title: Nasdaq sets closing record as tech shares rise despite higher bond yields
business.summary: The Nasdaq Composite closed at a record high on Oct. 5, gaining about 1% as Nvidia, Microsoft and other technology shares advanced while investors weighed falling oil prices and the start of quarterly earnings season. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones also rose. Stocks gained despite a sharp rise in Treasury yields: the 10-yea
business.content: The Nasdaq Composite closed at a record high on Oct. 5, gaining about 1% as Nvidia, Microsoft and other technology shares advanced while investors weighed falling oil prices and the start of quarterly earnings season. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones also rose. Stocks gained despite a sharp rise in Treasury yields: the 10-year yield reached 5.35%, its highest level since 2002, while weaker September jobs data reduced traders’ expectations of an October Federal Reserve rate increase. The Federal Reserve will release minutes from its September meeting on Wednesday, Oct. 7, and large U.S. banks are scheduled to begin reporting third-quarter results next week. Analysts expect S&P 500 earnings to grow more than 30% year over year, with AI-related companies accounting for much of the projected increase.
business.image_alt: Nasdaq sets closing record as tech shares rise despite higher bond yields

business.title: Trump allows dyed diesel on highways, defers tax through year-end
business.summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order Monday allowing red-dyed diesel, normally restricted to off-road use, on public roads through the end of 2026. The order does not eliminate the federal tax: it directs Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in consultation with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, to defer the exc
business.content: President Donald Trump signed an executive order Monday allowing red-dyed diesel, normally restricted to off-road use, on public roads through the end of 2026. The order does not eliminate the federal tax: it directs Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in consultation with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, to defer the excise tax on road use until year-end without interest or penalties, while the administration explores canceling the eventual payment. Trump said the change would lower fuel and goods costs for truckers, farmers and consumers. The move follows a record surge in diesel prices: the U.S. national average exceeded $6 a gallon in September for the first time, and prices peaked at about $6.50 last month. Diesel powers heavy freight vehicles, and its price affects the cost of goods transported by road. The White House cited the Russia-Ukraine war and a global shortage of refining capacity in its explanation. Its fact sheet also blamed refinery closures in Democratic-led states and did not mention Iran. The order directs federal agencies to coordinate access to dyed diesel and examine whether the deferred tax can be canceled. The tax deferral runs through Dec. 31, 2026.
business.image_alt: Trump allows dyed diesel on highways, defers tax through year-end

business.title: Brazilian assets rally as Flávio Bolsonaro gains election edge
business.summary: Brazilian stocks and the real surged on Monday after Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro finished ahead of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the first round of the presidential election. The Bovespa rose 7.85% to a record 207,190 points, while the real strengthened more than 4% against the dollar, moving below 5 reais per dolla
business.content: Brazilian stocks and the real surged on Monday after Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro finished ahead of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the first round of the presidential election. The Bovespa rose 7.85% to a record 207,190 points, while the real strengthened more than 4% against the dollar, moving below 5 reais per dollar from about 5.22 on Friday. Investors are betting Bolsonaro would pursue spending restraint, privatizations and tax cuts, easing concerns about Brazil’s public finances. Bolsonaro won 47.03% of valid votes to Lula’s 45.16%, setting up a runoff on Oct. 25 after polls had generally put Lula ahead in the first round. Bolsonaro’s Liberal Party also expanded its presence in Congress, which analysts say could help him advance reforms if he wins.
business.image_alt: Brazilian assets rally as Flávio Bolsonaro gains election edge

business.title: New York City lawmakers weigh AI safety rules after insider warnings
business.summary: New York City Council members questioned executives from Google, Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic on Oct. 5 as former employees warned that advanced AI could become difficult to control and called for stronger oversight. The hearing focused on a package of 10 proposed city bills, including a requirement for independent safet
business.content: New York City Council members questioned executives from Google, Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic on Oct. 5 as former employees warned that advanced AI could become difficult to control and called for stronger oversight. The hearing focused on a package of 10 proposed city bills, including a requirement for independent safety validation and a human-operated shutdown mechanism before companies could market, sell or deploy AI systems in the city. Former OpenAI and Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon said humanity was more likely than not to lose control of advanced AI on the industry’s current path. Former OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo warned that labs could mistakenly believe safety measures work when they do not. The company witnesses said forecasting catastrophic risks lacks a rigorous scientific method. None raised a hand when asked whether their company had insurance covering catastrophic AI risks. Other proposed measures would give whistleblowers a share of recovered fines, allow lawsuits over foreseeable harms from jailbroken tools and require city contractors to report AI safety incidents within 24 hours. Council Speaker Julie Menin said the hearing would inform lawmakers as they develop the legislation.
business.image_alt: New York City lawmakers weigh AI safety rules after insider warnings

science.title: Canadian analysis favors permanent standard time over daylight saving
science.summary: A review by Canadian researchers concludes that permanent standard time is likely healthier than permanent daylight saving time if governments end twice-yearly clock changes. Published in the Canadian Medical Association Journal, the analysis says morning light helps synchronize the body’s circadian clock, while shifti
science.content: A review by Canadian researchers concludes that permanent standard time is likely healthier than permanent daylight saving time if governments end twice-yearly clock changes. Published in the Canadian Medical Association Journal, the analysis says morning light helps synchronize the body’s circadian clock, while shifting winter daylight later could delay that signal. Under permanent daylight saving time, the latest winter sunrise would be 8:51 a.m. in Toronto and 9:40 a.m. in Calgary—an hour later than under standard time. The authors warn that darker mornings could affect sleep, mood, learning and productivity, while acknowledging that standard time brings earlier summer sunrises and winter sunsets. They urge governments choosing permanent daylight saving time to plan safety measures and monitor sleep, mental health, school absenteeism, injuries, physical activity and cardiovascular events.
science.image_alt: Canadian analysis favors permanent standard time over daylight saving

science.title: Record-strength El Niño threatens heat, drought and water supplies
science.summary: Daily sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific reached 3.08°C above the 1991–2020 average on Sept. 21 during the 2026 El Niño, exceeding the previous daily record of 3.02°C set in 2015. NOAA has not formally declared it a record event: its newer Relative Oceanic Niño index still ranks the
science.content: Daily sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific reached 3.08°C above the 1991–2020 average on Sept. 21 during the 2026 El Niño, exceeding the previous daily record of 3.02°C set in 2015. NOAA has not formally declared it a record event: its newer Relative Oceanic Niño index still ranks the 1997–98 El Niño as stronger, though a Sept. 10 forecast indicated that record could soon be surpassed. Scientists expect the current event to strengthen and peak in the next few months. El Niño shifts rainfall and heat patterns worldwide. A report from the University of Chicago’s Climate Impact Lab, cited by Science News Explores, estimates that ocean heat from the event could raise global land temperatures by about 1.2°C and contribute to more than 450,000 additional heat-related deaths by February. Vietnam’s agriculture ministry forecasts a 98% chance of very strong El Niño conditions from October through December, with risks of drought and saltwater intrusion extending into 2027.
science.image_alt: Record-strength El Niño threatens heat, drought and water supplies

science.summary: Researchers say they have identified why so-called “zombie cells” build up as people age, according to Medical Xpress and Nautilus. The headlines do not describe the proposed mechanism or the study’s methods. A related article in The Conversation examines diet and biological aging. Nautilus also examines whether the ce
science.content: Researchers say they have identified why so-called “zombie cells” build up as people age, according to Medical Xpress and Nautilus. The headlines do not describe the proposed mechanism or the study’s methods. A related article in The Conversation examines diet and biological aging. Nautilus also examines whether the cell buildup can be reversed.

science.title: Three scientists win 2026 Nobel medicine prize for optogenetics
science.summary: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the 2026 Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine on Oct. 5 for discoveries that established optogenetics, a method that uses light to study and control brain cell activity. Hegemann and Nagel identified the light-sensitive protein channelrhodopsin in single-celled algae
science.content: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the 2026 Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine on Oct. 5 for discoveries that established optogenetics, a method that uses light to study and control brain cell activity. Hegemann and Nagel identified the light-sensitive protein channelrhodopsin in single-celled algae, and Deisseroth adapted it into a light-controlled switch for nerve cells. The technique lets researchers identify which nerve cells in complex circuits control pain, social behavior, thirst, hunger, reward and attention, the Nobel committee said. The committee’s medicine chair, Per Svenningsson, said optogenetics offers new ways to map the brain. The 2026 prize announcements continue with physics on Oct. 6, chemistry on Oct. 7, literature on Oct. 8, peace on Oct. 9 and economics on Oct. 12; the laureates will receive their awards at ceremonies in December.
science.image_alt: Three scientists win 2026 Nobel medicine prize for optogenetics

science.title: Chinese four-winged dinosaur fossil points to separate origins of flight
science.summary: Researchers described a fossil of *Norellraptor barsboldi*, a feathered, four-winged dinosaur found in China, as evidence that flight-related features may have evolved independently in bird ancestors and microraptorines. The nearly complete skeleton is about 57 centimeters long, with feather traces around its forelimbs
science.content: Researchers described a fossil of *Norellraptor barsboldi*, a feathered, four-winged dinosaur found in China, as evidence that flight-related features may have evolved independently in bird ancestors and microraptorines. The nearly complete skeleton is about 57 centimeters long, with feather traces around its forelimbs, hindlimbs and tail. An evolutionary analysis found that the two lineages acquired similar flight-related traits in different sequences, supporting separate evolutionary pathways rather than a shared sequence of changes. The researchers caution that the fossil does not establish whether microraptorines used powered flight; scientists continue to debate whether they glided, flapped or did both.
science.image_alt: Chinese four-winged dinosaur fossil points to separate origins of flight

science.title: Perseverance finds evidence of at least three water episodes in Jezero rocks
science.summary: NASA’s Perseverance rover has found that water altered rocks in Jezero Crater’s Margin Unit on at least three occasions: first groundwater, then lower-pH water that may have been lake water, and finally hot fluids moving through fractures. Researchers cannot yet date the separate episodes. The resulting carbonate and s
science.content: NASA’s Perseverance rover has found that water altered rocks in Jezero Crater’s Margin Unit on at least three occasions: first groundwater, then lower-pH water that may have been lake water, and finally hot fluids moving through fractures. Researchers cannot yet date the separate episodes. The resulting carbonate and silica minerals can preserve chemical or microscopic traces, but the findings are not evidence that life existed on Mars. Perseverance has collected rock cores from the area for possible return to Earth, where researchers could examine them more closely in laboratories.
science.image_alt: Perseverance finds evidence of at least three water episodes in Jezero rocks

science.title: Moon will briefly hide Jupiter in rare October 6 alignment
science.summary: Before dawn on Tuesday, Oct. 6, the waning crescent Moon will pass directly in front of Jupiter, hiding the planet from observers across much of the eastern and central United States, Canada and the Caribbean. Parts of Mexico and Africa are also within the viewing region, though observers in parts of Africa will see th
science.content: Before dawn on Tuesday, Oct. 6, the waning crescent Moon will pass directly in front of Jupiter, hiding the planet from observers across much of the eastern and central United States, Canada and the Caribbean. Parts of Mexico and Africa are also within the viewing region, though observers in parts of Africa will see the event in daylight. The occultation will last up to about an hour, depending on location. In New York, it is expected to last from 4:23 to 5:27 a.m. EDT, and in Chicago from 3:22 to 4:17 a.m. CDT. Live Science says the next lunar occultation of Jupiter visible from North America is due on Nov. 27, 2037. No telescope is needed to see Jupiter disappear and reappear, though binoculars or a small telescope can provide a more detailed view.
science.image_alt: Moon will briefly hide Jupiter in rare October 6 alignment

science.title: Siberian lab worker dies of unknown pneumonia; 200 contacts monitored
science.summary: A worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Siberia died after developing pneumonia of unknown cause. Russian authorities placed nearly 200 people who may have had contact with her under medical observation. The woman was hospitalized on Sept. 29 and died early Oct. 2, according to reports cited by RFE/RL
science.content: A worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Siberia died after developing pneumonia of unknown cause. Russian authorities placed nearly 200 people who may have had contact with her under medical observation. The woman was hospitalized on Sept. 29 and died early Oct. 2, according to reports cited by RFE/RL. Local reports that she contracted pneumonic plague after a laboratory accident remain unconfirmed. Russia’s public-health agency, Rospotrebnadzor, said tests found no microorganisms linked to the woman’s work and that no pathogen-handling accident had occurred at the institute. Officials described the illness as pneumonia of unknown origin. Regional authorities said the situation was stable and no other institute employees had recently sought medical care. A hospital in Shelekhov was quarantined, and the United States said it was monitoring the case with the CDC and other agencies. The World Health Organization said the risk to public health appeared low based on unofficial information, but stressed that no cause of death had been officially confirmed.
science.image_alt: Siberian lab worker dies of unknown pneumonia; 200 contacts monitored

sports.title: Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott faces up to eight weeks out
sports.summary: Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott has withdrawn from England’s squad with a quadriceps injury expected to sideline him for six to eight weeks. The 23-year-old felt discomfort before playing 70 minutes in Saturday’s 7-0 Nations League win over Croatia and is now set to miss a demanding run of club fixtures. Bournemouth
sports.content: Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott has withdrawn from England’s squad with a quadriceps injury expected to sideline him for six to eight weeks. The 23-year-old felt discomfort before playing 70 minutes in Saturday’s 7-0 Nations League win over Croatia and is now set to miss a demanding run of club fixtures. Bournemouth are unhappy that Scott played despite the known issue. England manager Thomas Tuchel said the player and medical staff cleared him to play and that England took no risk. Scott will miss Tuesday’s game against the Czech Republic and could miss Bournemouth’s nine matches scheduled between October 10 and November 8. The club’s medical assessment will determine the length of his recovery.
sports.image_alt: Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott faces up to eight weeks out

sports.title: Australia to begin three-Test South Africa tour, first since 2018 scandal

sports.content: Australia begin a three-Test tour of South Africa on Friday, October 9, with the Durban opener marking their first Test visit there since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal. The teams are the top two in the world rankings, and South Africa beat Australia in last year’s World Test Championship final. South Africa won the 2018 series 3-1. Australia also have upcoming tours of India and England. Former South Africa captain Shaun Pollock expects fans to recall the scandal but not make the reception excessively hostile. Australia all-rounder Cameron Green is set to miss the first Test with an injury.

sports.content: Kansas City Chiefs receiver Tyquan Thornton will undergo ankle surgery this week and is expected to miss 12 to 16 weeks, while free-agent receiver Tyreek Hill could sign with an NFL team within days, his agent Drew Rosenhaus said Monday. Thornton dislocated his left ankle and tore ligaments; that recovery window could allow him to return late in the season or in the postseason. Kansas City has contacted Hill’s agent about a reunion. Rosenhaus said he planned to negotiate with multiple teams, and Hill is targeting a November return as he recovers from a serious knee injury. Thornton could miss most of the regular season; the Chiefs, 4-0, have a bye before hosting the Chargers on Oct. 18.

sports.content: England named a 23-player squad for the Rugby League World Cup on October 5, leaving out Leeds half-back Jake Connor and selecting Hull KR’s Mikey Lewis instead. Head coach Brian McDermott said Connor missed out by a “small margin” and that his decision came down to who best fits England’s game plan. England open against Tonga in Perth on October 17, then play France there on October 24 and Papua New Guinea in Wollongong on October 30. Four Wakefield players—Tom Johnstone, Jake Trueman, Mike McMeeken and Caleb Hamlin-Uele—were unavailable because they are scheduled for post-season surgery.

sports.content: Washington Capitals captain Alex Ovechkin announced on Oct. 5 that the 2026-27 season will be his last in the NHL, ending a 22-year career spent entirely with Washington. The 41-year-old holds the NHL record with 929 regular-season goals. He and his family decided this summer that it was time to leave the league, and he said he wants to stay healthy enough to play sports with his children as they grow up. Ovechkin told teammates before announcing his decision publicly, ahead of Wednesday’s home opener against the Pittsburgh Penguins. He urged the team to enjoy the season and make the playoffs. Washington missed the postseason last year, while Ovechkin played all 82 games and scored 32 goals. The Capitals open their home schedule against the rival Penguins as Ovechkin begins his final NHL season.

McVay said the staff would learn from the exchange and show mo
sports.content: Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay said Monday he had spoken with assistant coaches after videos showed them yelling at Philadelphia Eagles fans, banging on the glass of their stadium booth and making obscene gestures during Sunday’s 24-20 Rams comeback win. McVay said the staff would learn from the exchange and show more composure in emotional moments while still celebrating with the team. The incident followed Kyren Williams’ game-winning touchdown late in the fourth quarter at Lincoln Financial Field. A fan also threw a drink toward the coaches’ box, CBS Sports reported. Los Angeles erased a 10-point deficit in the final quarter to win. The Rams are scheduled to face the Buffalo Bills in Week 5.

sports.content: The Chicago White Sox and Tampa Bay Rays moved within one win of the American League Championship Series on Monday, taking 2-0 leads in their best-of-five Division Series. Chicago rallied past Cleveland 4-3, while Tampa Bay beat New York 5-2. Both teams can clinch on Wednesday, Oct. 7. Chicago trailed 2-1 before scoring three runs in the sixth inning and is now 4-0 in the postseason after sweeping Houston in the Wild Card round. Tampa Bay broke a tie with a four-run fifth inning, with Richie Palacios driving in two runs. New York’s four errors helped fuel the rally. The Yankees have scored only two runs in the series, both on Ben Rice home runs, and must win three straight to avoid elimination. In the National League, Milwaukee leads San Diego 2-0, while Atlanta and the defending champion Dodgers are tied 1-1. Chicago hosts Cleveland in Game 3 and Tampa Bay visits New York on Wednesday. The Brewers and Padres are scheduled to play Tuesday.

sports.title: Portugal coach Jesus leaves door open for Ronaldo return
sports.summary: Portugal coach Jorge Jesus says Cristiano Ronaldo can return to the national team if he wants, leaving the decision to the 41-year-old forward after he left camp on learning he would not start against Denmark. sports.content: Portugal coach Jorge Jesus says Cristiano Ronaldo can return to the national team if he wants, leaving the decision to the 41-year-old forward after he left camp on learning he would not start against Denmark. Ronaldo had been an unused substitute in the 2-1 Nations League win over Norway and departed after Jesus told him he would not start the next match. Jesus said he would speak with Ronaldo before announcing the next squad and wants him to decide how his international career ends. Portugal Football Federation president Pedro Proença called the episode a misunderstanding to be resolved internally and said Ronaldo remains eligible if technically fit. Ronaldo said he would explain his reasons for leaving “in due course”. Portugal won all four Nations League matches in the international window and secured a quarter-final place without him, with two group games remaining. Its next fixtures are at home to Denmark on November 14 and away to Wales three days later. Ronaldo’s return is expected to be discussed before the next squad announcement.
